And *secondly*, a wrath-fire from the receptivity of the flowed-out self-will, in which the love-fire becomes manifest; which wrath-fire is a ground of the eternal NATURE, and in the center of its inwardness, it is called an eternal darkness and pain. And yet, *both these fires are but one single ground*, and have been from eternity, and remain for eternity; but yet they separate themselves into two eternal origins, as is to be seen in fire and light.

### Question IV.—What was there prior to the Angels and the Creation?

*Answer.* (1.) There was God, with the two central fires, with the great powers, namely, an eternal, infinite generation of wonders, colors, and virtues. Therein did lie the angels and the soul of man, together with all creatures of this world, and of the inward angelical, spiritual world—as an <term>IDEA</term> or spiritual modeling, in which God from eternity has seen all his works. Not in a creature-formed kind and shape—that is, in a state of division—but in the form of the powers, according to how the Spirit of God played with itself.

(2.) In these *central fires* was the element (the *one element*), and both were but *one single* being, yet distinguished into two <term>principles</term>, like fire and light, as already shown.

(3.) But when the central fire of the self-will moved and introduced itself into a greater desire for its own visibility and formation, then the creation was effected. That is, when the eternal Will of God moved according to both fires, then the <term>IDEA</term> became image-like, to the praise of the wonders of God.

(4.) And in this motion the hellish foundation, God’s wrath, broke forth along with it, which God rejected from His working and shut up in the darkness. There it stands even to this day, like hungry jaws, full of desire for the creation, wishing also to be manifested in the form of a creature and in an image-like manner.

(5.) And this is the ground and cause that the throne-prince, Lucifer, turned himself away from God’s love into the central-fire of the wrath, where he intended to rule over God’s gentleness and love; and through this, he was cast out of the central love-fire, and lost his throne in the light, and now possesses hell, along with the damned souls. This hellish foundation in the curse of God’s wrath is a *center* of the visible world; and the same is called *SATAN*, of whom Christ says that he deceives the whole world, and is understood in the kingdom of darkness, where heat and cold are in conflict. (Enough for our school-fellows.)

### Question V.—What was the ground and substance out of which the Angels were created? What was that power in the Word of God which flowed out and became a creature?

*Answer.* (1.) The Scripture says of God, *You make the winds your ministers, and flames of fire your angels.* Psalm 104:4. In these words is contained the whole understanding; for with the word *ministers* is understood the image-like <term>IDEA</term>, namely, the spirit of the angels, out of the breathing of the Divine power and might, out of the Holy name of God.

(2.) And the phrase *fire-flames* signifies the central-fire of the eternal Nature, in which the substance of the creature stands, namely, the will of its own self-substance. This is now to be understood as follows:

(3.) The <term>IDEA</term> or the image of God has been a form of the Divine name, in the opening name of God, in which God from eternity has known all things; that is, an imagination of the divine will, where the will of the Abyss has shaped itself into a form, and yet it has been no creature, but only an <term>IDEA</term>, as an image is formed in a mirror. Thus has the imagination of the Divine power imaged itself in the flowing-out name of God.

(4.) But when God would have such an <term>IDEA</term> in a living creature—that is, in a state of self-desiring—then he moved and separated the central fire of the eternal Nature, whereby the <term>IDEA</term> became manifest in the fire, which was done through the breathing, or the *Yea*.

(5.) At the same time, the *Nay*, namely, the flowed-out will of its own receptivity, imaged itself together with the out-breathed *Yea*, so that the creature might stand in its own or self-will: which own or self-will is understood in the central fire—that is, in the properties of the fire—in which the creaturely life stands.

(6.) For if this had not been, then Lucifer would not have been able to separate himself in self-will from the Good and to fall. If he had had no own-will, then God’s power must have fallen; but thus

Though in God they are all equal, they are distinct in the outflow—that is, in Wisdom—for the sake of manifestation and wonders. Thus, there is a difference or distinction of the angelic *IDEA* in power, and one always has a greater power and might than the other, as well as a different virtue.

(10.) As the stars in the firmament are different, so are the angels, so that there may be a *harmony*—namely, a joy and knowledge of the divine powers.

(11.) Their true foundation lies in the thrones of the powers of God, and they are ministers everywhere within those thrones of power. For out of the thrones—that is, out of the Holy outflowing names of God, out of the eternal Unity—the *IDEA* has sprouted; therefore, there are distinctions and dominions among them.

(12.) Although they are all God’s ministers, every throne has its offices and legions with particular names, according to those very thrones and powers. Therefore, there are prince-angels among them, all according to the property of each throne; such power as the throne has, the prince-angel has as well. The others are ministers, not slaves, but free-will voices in the *harmony* of the throne, all for the praise of the *great God*.

(13.) The whole depth within and without the world is full of such thrones and dominions, yet not in the four elements, but in the pure element of the inward fire and light. They possess another *principium*—namely, another world—which is indeed present within this world, but in a different quality and another <term>chaos</term>.

(14.) Understand the foundation of the angels in this way: they are from the essence of both inward eternal fires. Their powers are the great outflowing Names of God; all of them originated from the *Yes* and were introduced into the *No*, so that the powers might become manifest. Thus, there must be an object in which a distinction can exist.

(15.) The name <term>IACHIEL</term> is the distinction of the *IDEA* of the *virtue*, from which flows <term>ELIEL</term> and the Holy Names according to the Divine property, which are many; but all of them flow out of the divine *senses*—to hint at it for the reader.

(16.) But the names of the prince-angels, which in *sense* bear the R, T, or S—their power stands in the strength of the fire’s might, from the high name <term>TETRAGRAMMATON</term> (<term>IEHoVaH</term>). They are the princes over the astral *elementum* and over the four *elements*, for they have their dwelling in the interior *elements*, from which the four *elements* have flowed and still continue to flow.

(17.) Though indeed there are still exterior princes who dwell in the four elements and are called astral spirits—namely, *ascendants*—who also have their properties in the world but are not like the inward ones. For they have another <term>chaos</term> of an exterior kind, about which (Note Well) nothing further is to be mentioned here, out of respect for potential abuse and superstition.

(18.) If we would consider and truly understand the powers and virtues of the angels, and not cling to dead pictures or images, as foolish *reason* always does, then we have only to consider the *spirits of the letters*—in what sense and power each one stands—and then the uniting of these *letter-spirits*, from which the word or understanding originates; thus we have the whole basis, with *Yes* and *No*, which is the entire foundation.

(19.) For just as the words with the spirits of the letters are distinct, so too is their distinction in the creaturely, image-like form; human kingdoms are like this, as is everything called a creature. They are all nothing else but Divine *senses* from both central fires, like joined words of the Divine Powers.

(20.) Just as the entire alphabet constitutes the full understanding of all things, so is God’s *Word* the sole understanding of all things, and the angels are *its letters*.

(21.) The Prince-angels signify the letters—namely, the thrones—and the ministering angels signify the joining of the *senses*, who allow themselves to be used for the *harmony* of the divine understanding, to the praise of God.

(22.) Just as the force and power for the distinction of the *senses* lie in the letters, so too does the greatest power lie in the throne-angels. The others are like the joining of the letters for distinction and are joined powers; as the tree is in its branches, so too is their order and government to be understood. For all generations in the four elements, together with men, exist in such a form; every generation also has its superiors, all of which is a figure of the inward, spiritual world.

(23.) If man were not so completely shut up in the *No*, so that he could understand what powers he carries in his mouth and what force exists there, he would greatly rejoice in it. But he cannot understand that because of the curse which lies before it, for he would misuse it. Let the curse be removed from him, and then he may see.

(24.) For he carries the power of all things balanced in his mouth. If he had the *faith* to adjust or form these powers, then he would have the basis of all mysteries and might perform wonders like the angels. The Scripture also testifies to this: *If you had faith as a grain of mustard seed, then you might be able to say to the mountain, cast yourself into the sea.* Also, *the Word is near you, even in your mouth and in your heart* (Matthew 17:20-21; Deuteronomy 30:11; Romans 10:8; Mark 16:17-18).

(25.) And this is, as mentioned above, for those who are of our school, and no further, out of respect for—

### Question VI.—*What is the office and activity of the Angels; and why did God's power introduce itself into images or figures?*

**Answer.** (1.) Just as we humans on earth rule all things—namely, the whole of what can be perceived—through the distinction of words, so also does God—namely, the eternal mind of the one and only power—work and rule with such image-like words in Wisdom.

(2.) The angels are simply imaged powers of the Word of God; for man's mind is a reflex-image, or <term>ectype</term>, of the eternal power of God.

(3.) For all senses come out of the mind, and out of the senses come right thoughts—that is, a conclusion or imagination—from which the <term>lubet</term> <note>good-pleasure or divine inclination</note> or good-pleasure exists. This <term>lubet</term> enters into a state of being, from which the perceptible desire arises, and out of that, the operation proceeds.

(4.) In the same way, God is the eternal mind, that is, the understanding; and yet there would be no distinction within it if it did not flow forth from Himself. His out-flowings are the powers, just as the senses are in man; and the powers introduce themselves into an imagination, in which stands the <term>angelical IDEA</term>. This imagination brings itself into a longing for perceptibility; this is the <term>Yea, A</term>, and the longing brings itself into desire, which is the ground of self-receptiveness—namely, the <term>Nay</term>. The desire brings itself into properties, even unto fire, out of which the Light springs. Thus, these properties of desire are divine thoughts, to be understood in two <term>centris</term> <note>centers</note>—namely, in the <term>Yea and the Nay</term>.

(5.) The <term>Yea</term> is divine, and the <term>Nay</term> is the selfhood of Nature—namely, the perceptibility of the desire. This desire for perceptibility has become a work (or figures)—namely, angels—which are nothing other than God's thoughts, according to love and wrath—namely, a manifestation of His mind and will.

(6.) Not that there are thoughts in God Himself, but in His out-flowing, desiring will, which introduces itself into fire and light for perceptibility.

(7.) And just as man, with his senses and thoughts, rules the world and all creatures, so God—namely, the eternal Unity—rules all things through the instrumentality of the angels; only the power and the work are of God. They are His work-instruments, with which He expresses Himself and moves, whereby and through which He manifests the eternal powers and wonders, and introduces them into a love-play.

(8.) They are altogether nothing other than strings in the great harmony of divine joyfulness, in the song and sound of the powers; and all of them are workers of the wonders of God—namely, formers of the powers and of the Holy Names of God.

(9.) Just as we humans, with our mouths, make the powers of the <term>sensuum</term> <note>senses</note> formal in articulate, sounding words, so their labor is also a simple forming of divine powers and forms.

(10.) For whatever they will and desire is brought into imagery and forms by their imagination—which are mere <term>ideæ</term>, just as the divine powers formed themselves into such <term>IDEAS</term> before the creation of the angels. Their modeling is likewise accordingly.

(11.) And herein lies the <term>HOLY CABALA</term> of the changes or variations, and the great joy in which the divine Wisdom and Science become imaged and formed through the spirits of the central fire and light. There is such a joy of knowledge in this that they eternally bow and humble themselves out of great joy and knowledge before such Highness, so that the <term>Nay</term> might not gain dominion over them, and that they might not be deprived of such honor and glory.

(12.) Their food is a creating, or an in-drawing desire for the Unity of God, from which their central fire receives the balsam, so that the fierce wrath might not awaken. Therefore, they also live eternally in resigned humility, so that the <term>Nay</term> might not elevate itself (as happened with the devils); the fall of Lucifer stands as a mirror to them.

(13.) Understand us rightly now: the whole creation of the inward and outer world (namely, in the holy, pure element and in the four elements) is a simple imaging and formation of the divine powers, but according to both central fires—namely, in the <term>Yea and Nay</term>. It is nothing other than one outflow proceeding from another, even to the grossest matter or compaction of earth and stones.

(14.) For the visible world is nothing other than the out-flowing Word with both the central fires, which have again created for themselves a <term>subjectum</term> with the outward elementary fires, in which the outward creatures live.

(15.) The more deeply we penetrate into the power of a thing, the closer we come to the Deity, as is to be understood in metals and vegetables, as well as in all living creatures. For the most outward are the four <term>elementa</term>; the next is the astral <term>corpus</term>; the third is the <term>quinta essentia</term>, or the ground of the out-flowing holy element; the fourth is the <term>tinctur</term>—namely, the highest power of the out-flowing Word, in which both the inward central fires lie in one single <term>subjecto</term>; and after this, the pure Deity is understood.

(16.) If we would only wake once from the <term>Adamical sleep</term> and look around us, we might indeed see wonders. If the earth were not so dear to us, then we might well see heaven (as it is understood to be ours).

(17.) This, then, is the conclusion concerning the activity of the angels: they are co-playmates of the divine joy, and are members and branches of the great trees of the Divine Names, upon which the heavenly fruits grow. They receive their nourishment from the sap of their trees—namely, every angel from his throne; and as the throne (the Name of God) is, so is also the office of the angels belonging to it. Yet all the trees together are but one tree, which is GOD.

The wise 'Heathens' understood the <term>subjectum</term>—namely, the <term>ectypes</term> of such thrones—and honored them as gods, but they did not have the true foundation of the inward nature. ### *Question VII.— What induced Lucifer to lust against God and turn himself away from the Good?*

*Answer* (1.) His *own-receptiveness*, that is, the *Nay*, induced him. The out-flowing will in the central-fire of the eternal Nature is the cause of it; that will lifted itself up in him and desired to image the Divine power within the fire’s might.

(2.) He desired to prove or experiment with the properties of the eternal Nature, and would not remain in resignation, but wanted to dominate in and with the Holy name of the throne.

(3.) Yet the cause which moved him to such a desire is the throne of which he was—and indeed remains eternally—a prince, according to his property of the fire’s might; but according to the Holy name of the light’s power, he has not remained there, but rather according to the darkness.

(4.) When the movement toward the creation of the angels occurred, then the out-flowing will of his own-receptiveness elevated itself, and the properties stood in great activity, and wanted to be creaturely.

(5.) In these properties, the creaturely will of *Lucifer* created. When he apprehended the omnipotence within them and found the *wonder-working Power* in himself, then his creaturely will elevated itself according to the fire’s might, and abused or misused the Holy name in himself. He would not abide in resignation, but wanted to dominate over the thrones, and so he severed himself from the Unity.

(6.) He wanted to dominate with the *Nay* over the *Yea*, for the *Nay* elevated itself in him and despised the *Yea*, because the potential for separation and form-giving stood in the *Nay*; therefore the creaturely will wanted to dominate in the *Nay*, that is, in the transmutation, and severed itself from the Unity of God, entering into the receptiveness of the properties.

(7.) And instantly the properties in him became individually manifested—namely, the cold fire, as well as the sharpness, acidity, hardness, bitterness, thorniness, hostility, and anguish of the fire. Thus he became an enemy of all love, humility, and gentleness, for the foundation of God’s wrath grasped or possessed that false will.

---

### *Question VIII.— How could an Angel become a devil, or what is a Devil? In what essence and substance does he stand after the fall?*

*Answer* (1.) It is not to be understood as if the Holy name, in which Lucifer was a throne-angel, has become a devil in him; much less the central love-fire, which is the power of the Light. No, that cannot be.

(2.) For when Lucifer brought his desire into self-might, he then severed himself from the Will of God, whereupon the Holy name severed itself from him, and the Light in his fire-life was extinguished. For he severed himself from the Unity, which is a balsam of the fire, in which the fire conceives its glance of the Light.

(3.) Thus there now remained in him nothing other than the *Nay*, an imaged *creature*, and the *Yea* departed from him. For the *Nay* divorced itself from the *Yea* in its own self-willing, and would not be under the *Yea*—that is, under the divine breathing of the Unity—but wanted to be its own breathing.

(4.) Thus he remained a mere cold, hard, sharp, pointed, bitter, stinging, poisonous, anxious, and painful *fire-essence*, in which the central-fire stands in mere strife, hunger, and thirst, and can attain no refreshing.

(5.) For if *Lucifer* were to become an angel again, then he would have to drink again from the Unity and Love of God, and his fire-life would have to be killed by Love and transmuted into humility. But the hellish foundation in the devils will not do this, and indeed cannot do it, for there is in them all no longer any inclination or desire for humility or repentance.

(6.) Their whole life is nothing other than the hellish foundation, a fountain-spring or source of the wrath of God, a mere poison and stench, a dying torment! Whenever they hear talk of *love* and *humility*, they flee away, for love is the death of their false life.

(7.) They indeed have an eternal sorrow for their lost inheritance—namely, for the Good—yet they can have no belief that they might receive grace; for their belief is an eternal doubting.

(8.) They are severed from God; therefore they curse or shun God’s power and will, which is an intolerable thing to them. For if they were touched by the Holy power of God, then that would enervate or deflower <note>to strip of power or virtue</note> them, because it mortifies the self-will; and the self-will does not want that, for it would lose its might and power.

(9.) Thus has *Lucifer*, who was a throne-prince, forsaken the Holy name in him, and the self-will—namely, the creature—has elevated itself on high: understand the central fire-life, according to the properties of the eternal Nature.

(10.) Thus he has trifled away the Divine image, or the <term>IDEAM</term>, so that it has become dumb and inoperative; it is like a withered tree, without divine power, a figure without motion. He is eternally ashamed of this, for within him stands an *angelic character*, and yet this is no longer of an angelic kind or form. He has lost the original image of God and has become like the venomous worms and beasts whose life consists of poison.

(11.) The devils have acquired such a deformity of shape according to their various properties, for their properties are quite distinct and different, all according to the foundation of the hellish essence. They also have their princely dominions among themselves, all according to their properties; for there are pride-devils, avarice-devils, enchantment or witchcraft-devils, and many others like them, acting as a <term>contrarium</term> <note>an opposite or contrary force</note> against God’s Wisdom and Truth.

(12.) Every divine Good power has a <term>contrarium</term> in the hellish foundation—that is, in the *Nay*—so that the *Yea*, namely the Truth, might be recognized; and thus the darkness—namely the foundation of God’s wrath—has become image-like, or creaturely (*N.B.*), in the devils.

(13.) But yet it may be asked, how is it possible that out of a beautiful, holy angel, an ugly, wrathful devil has come to be?

(14.) This occurs through the two eternal central-fires, in which the will stands in the properties; when the one divorces itself from the other, then it is already done. This is also done in man, and it is what destroys a good man.

It describes how the demonic realm serves as a contrary force to God's light, emphasizing that the self-will's refusal of humility makes their fallen state eternal.</summary>

## **Question IX.**—*Seeing that God is omnipotent, why did he not resist Lucifer, but allowed it to happen?*

**Answer.** (1.) When fire and light are once divorced, then there is a great enmity of one against the other; just as water and fire are enemies, and neither of them desires the other anymore, for one is the death of the other. But as long as they stand together in one single growing life, in one single ground, they love one another and exist in great joy together. This is also how the devil and God are to be understood. God no longer desires the devil, and the devil also no longer desires God:
(2.) But if it is asked, why did God not prevent him during the movement? It is answered: God did give him his Love, and so did prevent him, just as he also prevented Adam. But the eternal central fire, namely God’s wrath, would not have it; that fire within them would sever itself into its own kind.
(3.) Here we are to distinguish between God’s love and wrath. They are indeed both called GOD; but God, insofar as he is the eternal Good, is not the wrath—the wrath has another <term>principium</term> <note>principle or beginning</note>. In the Love-fire they are indeed one, but in the separation they are two. And seeing they are both eternal, without beginning, they therefore also have an eternal will, and the one cannot kill the other, but each continues in itself eternally. They are nothing other than a twofold power and are two <term>centra</term> <note>centers</note>, yet they come originally out of the Unity, out of one ground.
(4.) Therefore, when I say of God’s love that it is omnipotent, over all and in all—this is done according to the will of the *Yea*, namely the Light; and if the *Nay* gives its will to it, then the *Yea* changes the *Nay* into its power and love, and yet they remain two central wills within one another, yet in only one ground, in one Love and desire; otherwise the wrathful God would not be omnipotent if the Love held him solely in its omnipotence. There is no other but one God, yet the Love would not be manifest, and no Love would be known without the wrath.
(5.) Therefore the Love yields itself up to the wrath-fire, so that it may be a love-fire. But if the wrath severs itself from the love into self-receptivity, then the Love does not hinder it with force, otherwise it would follow that God was at odds with himself.
(6.) Thus the *Nay*, namely God’s wrath, in the fallen angels, has gone into a separation from the Love, into a self-dominion; and this is also a wonder, and moreover Good: so that the other angels have a looking-glass or warning so that the self-will does not elevate itself. Also, so that there is an eternal joy and praise of God, that they do not live in such a fire's essence, and thereupon they turn their desire all the more into the Unity of God and remain standing in resignation and humility, which is in the divine harmony.
(7.) Now when it is said here of the will of God’s wrath that it broke itself off from the Love and wanted to be form-like, that must not be understood as being *outside* the creature. It was no strange will in the apostate angels which had not then been form-like, but rather the wrathful God in the formed creature, which creature before was form-like; otherwise their whole <term>locus</term> <note>place or station</note> would have been an apostasy. Yet that it is not so appears by this: that they were thrust out of their thrones.
(8.) We must not lay the fault of the fall upon God, but only upon the formed power in the creature, according to the *Nay*. This has thrown it away, so that it has become a lie; not God, but the creature; not the unformed power wherein the Love burns, but the throne according to its receptivity and selfhood. And as their king and prince did, so likewise did all his legions.
(9.) For when God’s wrath hardens a creature, a strange, fierce wrath does not then enter into it to harden it, but its own fierce wrath does that; which is why a sentence or judgment passes upon it. For if God forced it to evil, then no judgment could be passed upon it, for it would be doing only what God wanted; but instead, it does what God does *not* want it to do, and therefore it comes into judgment or condemnation.
(10.) *Reason* babbles much indeed concerning God and his omnipotence, but it understands little of God and his being, what and how he is. It separates the soul totally from God, as if he were a separate being, and it does not know what an angel and a soul are. And this is the great misfortune of the blindness of reason: that men wrangle, dispute, and never at all come to the foundation.

## **Question X.**—*What did the Devil desire, whereupon he divorced himself from God’s love?*

**Answer.** (1.) He desired to be an artist. He saw the creation and understood the ground; whereas he himself wanted to be a self-God and rule with the central fire’s might in all things, and form himself with all things, also forming himself in all shapes, so that he might be what he wanted, and not what the Creator wanted. Indeed, this is still to this day the greatest joy of the devils: that they can transmute themselves and bring themselves into many images, and thus perform phantasms.
(2.) He wanted to be a fool, and that is what he has become; but he did not know how it would be if the Light should extinguish in him. Just as Adam also did not know how it would be when he should feel heat and cold; when also the central fire, together with the properties, should awake in him; and that he should fall out of the balance <note>temperature</note> and lose the central light-fire: Adam did not know this.
(3.) The devil wanted to be a Lord in the *Nay* and possess another <term>principium</term>, namely the power of the separation in the ground of the figure-like forming. Subjection did not please him, but highness did; he despised humility and sweetness or meekness—namely Love and Truth—and did not want to be in the Unity, but in the multiplicity.
(4.) He wanted to work with his own name, that is, with the central fire’s power, and not with God’s name from his own throne; he set the *Nay* above the *Yea*. Thus he became an enemy of God, and a *liar* and murderer of the good forming of the good powers; he desired to destroy whatever the working of God formed, so that he might represent his own working and forming.
(5.) The magic ground of the omnipotence pleased him; for which he revolted and spoke against the *Yea*, because this was not a fire’s working in his <term>centro</term> <note>center</note>, and because he saw that the *Yea*, namely the outflowing of the Unity, introduced itself into the fire’s <term>centro</term> as a Light and working Love. Lucifer's fall was driven by his desire to be his own creator and ruler, choosing the "Nay" of self-assertion and multiplicity over the "Yea" of divine unity.</summary>

Therefore, he supposed that the nature of the fire was stronger and greater than the gentleness of the Unity—namely, the imaged Names in the opening Unity—which he intended to bring into his fire's power as he pleased; yet God had not created him for such a will.

(6.) Therefore, seeing that he forsook God's ordinance, the Holy opening Name of God severed itself from him and continued in the Unity. Lucifer remained in the properties of the central fire, dwelling within himself. Yet he still stood in his princely throne, where the Holy name of God had imaged itself into a throne; however, he was no longer an angel with his legions, but a horrible mask-like image and a monster.

(7.) For when the Light went out in him, then the darkness and the cold sharpness of the fierceness became manifest in him, and he *instantly* became an enemy of God and of all the angelic hosts.

### Question XI.— *What was the struggle between Michael and the Dragon? What are Michael and the Dragon; and how is the victory and casting out achieved?*

*Answer.* (1.) Michael is the exalted name of the divine figure of this throne in which Lucifer was a prince. It is that which severs itself from the "No"—that is, from the lie—in which name and power Lucifer should have worked together with God. It was the might and power of the strong Love of God in this throne, and it remains so eternally. Also, he himself is the throne according to the Divine figure in the Unity—not as a creature, but as a figure of the power of God in the opening or moving of the Unity.

(2.) This Name was afterwards ordained for man when the Unity moved once more with the flowing out of JE-SUS. For this reason, the devil became an enemy of men, because they shall possess his throne; therefore, he desires to have men in his kingdom.

(3.) But the Dragon is the hellish foundation in its manifestation, into which Lucifer and his legions had imaged themselves. This foundation, along with the throne of prince Lucifer, had elevated itself—namely, the central-fire kingdom according to its receptiveness. This also is no creature, but the figure of God’s wrath, according to the way it is separated from the Unity and Love.

(4.) It is the self-will of the power of the wrath, which cannot easily be expressed with imagery. It is also the fierceness, a source and essence of heat, cold, hardness, acid sharpness, sting, bitter anguish, and woe—namely, the perceptibility, the first <term>principium</term> <note>principle</note>, a mere hunger and thirst, a desire for vanity and lies, a stench of poison and death-quality.

(5.) This fire is like a sulfurous fire which burns in stench and poison, for it is the dying death-anguish—namely, death and hell—which became manifest in the apostasy of *Lucifer*.

(6.) But the *SATAN* who seduces the whole world, as Christ says, is now this false will of the self, the first <term>principium</term> <note>principle</note>—namely, the will of hell, a ground of lies and contradictions, a leading away from the good, a universal spirit of the hellish foundation. Yet he is *no creature*, but the false mind in the hellish foundation—namely, the hellish science <note>knowledge or systematic understanding</note>.

(7.) And there are also devils of such properties and names, who are also princes in their legions, for they have imaged themselves in the hellish property.

(8.) This ground is their life and holds them captive within itself; and as the properties of the hellish foundation are manifold, so also there are such princes among them, ruling in those same properties.

(9.) Thus also *Belial* is the source of lust, uncleanness, and disorder.

(10.) *Beelzebub* is a source of idolatry and false imagery.

(11.) *Asmodus* is a spirit of fury or madness, and so forth. All these are qualities of the hellish foundation, yet there are also such created spirits within it.

(12.) But *Lucifer* is the fountain-source of pride—namely, of ambition.

(13.) All these properties were also awakened in man after the fall, when he turned himself away from God, and they have imaged themselves within man.

(14.) These same things are now the *Dragon*, the *old Serpent*, with whom MICHAEL—namely, the figure of the Divine power—fought and cast him out of the Holy names, together with his legions; and in man, the name JE-SUS strives against this Dragon.

(15.) This struggle is not a created, physical being. Indeed, it has gone forth against the imagery-like domination of the false, lying spirits that would rule and domineer in the Divine Names; it is a struggle between "Yes" and "No," between the image-like wrath and image-like Love, between the first and second <term>principium</term> <note>principle</note>.

(16.) In this struggle, the Divine character of the <term>IDEÆ</term> <note>Ideas or eternal forms</note> must overcome if it is to be an angel. In this struggle Adam fell, and in this struggle the name JE-SUS, in the assumed humanity, obtained the victory over this Dragon in the wilderness when he was tempted for forty days, and at last in death totally overcame him.

(17.) This struggle was with Moses on Mount *Sinai*, in the Father’s property, in the fire, where he remained for forty days. There Israel was tested to see if they could and would abide in the property of the Father, but when that was not possible, then Israel fell away and made themselves an idol-god—namely, the golden calf. Because of this, the tables of the Law were broken to signify that the human will of the self could not prevail against the foundation of the wrath, but it must now be broken and put to death, and through death be introduced again into the Holy names.

(19.) Therefore Christ had to die and lead the human will through death, through hell, and through this foundation, for the self-receptiveness of the self-will cannot exist in God. For if a will is to exist in God, it must be imperceptible and impassive, so that it may be able to dwell in the fire and yet not be consumed by the fire.

(20.) Just as the sun penetrates through all the elements and kindles itself in them, yet its light continues free in itself; or just as the fire glows through the iron, yet it does not become iron, but the iron is only an <term>objectum</term> <note>object</note> in which the fire elevates and inflames itself; so also must the *will* be *pure* which God’s Unity shall possess, so that there is no self-receptiveness in it.

(21.) For as soon as it passes into self-receptiveness, then such a dragon—namely, the hellish foundation—is manifest in it. It must penetrate thoroughly through the wrath-fire and only inflame itself in the fire, without self-receptiveness. When two clear essences would abide in one single ground,

(22.) Thus may love and wrath stand undivorced in only one ground, and be completely one original thing; and thus are we to consider God and the holy angels.

(23.) Now understand this Question in this way: the power of the throne—namely, the *Yea* and *Nay*, God's love and the imaged wrath of the eternal Nature of the central fire-will—have striven one against the other. *Lucifer* sat within this power with his angels and wanted to be a Lord; he was thus the cause that this central fire-will shaped itself into a den of the Dragon—that is, into a hellish foundation. God permitted this so that he might punish the apostate angel and hold him captive within it, to hinder him from further disturbing the creation.

### **Question XII.**—*How are men to consider the eternal counsel of God in Divine Contemplation, as St. Paul speaks concerning it in 1 Cor. 2:7—10 and Ephes. 1:11; which does not stand in man's ability as a creature, and yet is possible? How may a person, in true reality, come to see and understand such a ground of the deep Unity?*

Answer. (1.) We have introduced this question because the unenlightened mind holds it impossible to be able to know such secret mysteries; and being itself unable to apprehend them, it blasphemes, ascribing such knowledge to the devil. Therefore, out of love for our fellow-creatures, we will expound the matter a little, to see if any may become able to see and understand this deep sense.

(2.) Reason proceeds in mere imagination in a creaturely way, and supposes that God, in his Trinity, had consulted with himself about what he would create, and how it would and should go with it. Based on this, reason determines the fall of Lucifer and of Adam within a certain limit, claiming that God foreknew it and therefore had ordained it by his predestined purpose, and so forth. But reason's mere thinking is not the ground. God did not need to consult with himself about anything, for he himself is the counsel; the high outflowing Names of the powers—namely, the *wonder-doing-Word*—is the counsel of God. There is also no predestined purpose concerning anything, for the origin of all things lies in the idea, in eternal imaging; not like an imaged substance, but in a perpetual ideal imaging, where God's Love and Wrath—namely, the two central-fires of the powers—stand in a continually enduring love-wrestling. Where, in such wrestling of the powers, the *wonder-doing-Word* images itself in figures, which are mere reflex-images of the Holy names and powers, and are called IDEAS.

(3.) On the other side, the powers of the eternal Nature also image themselves according to the manner of the forms of the fire—namely, in a dark, sharp, hard, fierce, prickly-stinging, bitter, anxious, fiery, and cold manner. These are not creatures, but an imaging of the powers in the Nay—that is, in God's wrath; and yet they are continually penetrated or possessed with the *Yea* and the central-light, and changed into a Love-play, as if an evil thing were becoming a good thing, or a damned soul or angel were becoming a good, holy angel.

(4.) Such imaging of the IDEÆ has indeed been from eternity, where the Spirit of God has seen all things—what there should and could come to be when such imagings should be brought forth as creatures. Yet it does not come from a divine consultation of the Holy Name, but exists in the outflowing free will, according to both the central-fires of the powers, where the powers create and image themselves. The self-will images itself in the Nay—namely, in the fierce fire's kind—and the *Yea*, or outbreathing of the Unity, forms itself in the Light; and both these figures stand within one another in only one ground. In the *Yea* stands the Holy Name of the love of God, and in the Nay stands the name of the wrath of God. There the *Yea*, in the Holy Name of the divine Love, wrestles with the *Nay* (that is, with the outflown will of self-receptiveness) for the victory, and yet it is nothing other than a Love-play. For the Light penetrates the imaging of the darkness, by which this imaging is set into a joyful triumph; thus there is an eternal overcoming of the Dragon in God's wrath, and yet it is nothing other than a sport of both the central-fire-wills.

(5.) And here is the purpose of God, of which the Scripture speaks, and yet it stands in the own-will or self-will. God, inasmuch as he is, and is called God—or rather Deity—has no need of any figure, but the powers are necessary for the overcoming.

(6.) And here is also the ground of the devils, where the self-will—that is, the *Nay*—strove in an image-like manner against the *Yea*, and departed from the *Yea*, having divorced itself by its own self-motion and become a devil—namely, an enemy against the *Yea*—and entered into its own image-like dominion.

(7.) In this ground, we also see how *Michael* has striven against this Dragon and the imaged false wills; in these false wills, the *Yea*—namely, the Holy name—was still present in the beginning when they were angels. But the self-will of the central-fire's own receptiveness severed itself from the *Yea* within itself, and therefore it was thrust out by the *Yea* in the name *Michael*.

(8.) This is also set before us in Holy Scripture, both by the prophet *Micah* and by king *Saul*, when an evil spirit from the Lord entered into *Saul*, and also into the prophet *Zedekiah* and his companions. Also when the Lord said:

> *Who shall persuade Ahab, that he may go up and fall at Ramoth-Gilead? And one said on this manner, and another said on that manner. And then came forth a spirit and stood before the Lord, and said, I will persuade him. And the Lord said unto him, Wherewith? And he said, I will go forth, and be a lying spirit in the mouth of all his prophets. And he said, Thou shalt persuade him, and prevail also; go forth, and do so.* 1 Kings 22:20, 22.

This same Lord was now the Wrath of God, which burned over Israel, as is to be seen in many places of the Scripture, especially in *Moses* and in the prophets, where the Lord threatened them in his fire's might that he would devour them. <note>Understand that the Scriptures do not always mean the same thing by the word God, Lord, or Lord God; for example, this Lord is not the same as that mentioned in St. James 1:13.</note>

(9.) Thus we now rightly understand in this ground that such pouring forth of God's wrath comes out of such a foundation; for in the Holy name of God—namely, in the *centre* of the Light—there is no wrathful will, but only love, which is God himself.

(10.) But in the *Nay*, that is in the fire’s might, exist such beams of wrath; and these are the evil spirits in Saul, and in the false prophets, and also in the Babylonian strife of the sects and parties, regarding opinions in religion. In these, they do not purely and sincerely love God, clinging only to him, but will only follow after inventions and reasoning; and thereupon such sources of error, and such evil contentious spirits rise up out of the fiery soul, which has sprung forth out of this ground of the eternal central-fire, and become a creature.

(11.) These sources are mere evil spirits from the *Lord* <note>Likely referring to a specific dominion or manifestation of divine power</note> of God’s Wrath, sprung forth out of the self-will of their own receptiveness, and are true heretics, or cast-out spirits, as the sects reproachfully call each other. By this we see that they strive merely for the victory of their own images, and in the latter would continually overcome the Holy name, namely, the out-flowed Word of God; for they strive only about the letter, in the same way as the inward strife occurs and comes to pass between the *Yea* and *Nay*, that is, between the two eternal principles.

(12.) And in this strife, the holy name JE-SUS sank itself down into humanity, so that it might overpower such a source of the Dragon and the wrath of God, and release poor man from the will of the *Nay*; and so now in this strife he rules over all his enemies, namely over sin, death, the devil, and hell, as the Scripture says, *until these his enemies (all of whom are enemies of the kingly and princely throne of Michael, because they have been thrust out of it) be laid under his feet as a footstool*, and this dominion and imaging in this throne ceases.

(13.) By this, enough is shown to those who are of the true theosophic fraternity, whose understandings are enlightened by God; and we intend this in love to all. It is the highest *arcanum* <note>secret or mystery</note> which God opens to us, and the very last, for those who can understand it. But for the scorners, so long as they persist in being such, we have written nothing; rather, we seal it with the eternal will, so that it shall be understood by no rash-judging, self-willed, blind scorner. Amen.

(14.) But now how we may really understand such depth of the Deity, and search all things, according to what St. *Paul* says of it, that *the Spirit searches all things, even the deep things of God*, 1 Cor. 2:10, and that the natural, rational man in self-ability, namely the own-will, apprehends nothing, and yet that this is apprehensible in man, understand it as follows:

(15.) Man is an image of the Being of all beings, a true image of God, according to Love and Wrath. *For first*, the soul is the eternal central-fire of the self-will, for out of that must all creatures come, and not out of the pure Deity.

(16.) And *secondly*, the soul-spirit is the central Light-fire, sprung forth out of the eternal IDEA of the power of God, and is supernatural; therefore it is also a temple of the Holy Spirit, in which Christ dwells, and feeds the soul with his flesh and blood, that is, with divine and human balsam, in which the death and wrath of God has become broken: whereupon there remains such divine balsam in the Spirit of the soul essentially, as Christ says, *Whosoever eats my flesh and drinks my blood, abides in me and I in him.* John 6:56.

(17.) But *thirdly*, the outward body is of the outer world, out of the four elements and the astral spirit, which outer dominion rules the outward life; for which outer dominion the Adamical soul longed or lusted, and for the sake of it severed its will from the Unity of God, and introduced it into the dominion of this world. There the will in itself became captive by the Dragon of God's wrath, and turned into a monster, when the true spirit died or faded away, so that the light of God was extinguished to it, and the IDEA became dumb and inoperative.

(18.) Which spirit the *Idea*, JE-SUS, namely an efflux from the divine Unity, came to assist, and introduced again the light of Love into the poor soul.

(19.) When this name JE-SUS, which was called CHRIST when he assumed humanity, entered into the poor apostate soul and penetrated it with this beam of God's Unity, then the eternal *idea*, namely the true Spirit, became living and movable again in such balsam of Love; then the light again shone in the eternal darkness of the soul, and the *Nay* was reunited with the *Yea*, where then *Michael* in the strife stood against the Dragon, namely the name of the throne in *Christo Jesu*.

*(20.) In this light the soul sees again into its native country, which it had at first, namely into its original, out of which it sprang forth; for the Name of God is in it, and works in the spirit. Here it stands in the contemplation of God, and may search out all things; yet not in self-motion and its own will, but when the Name of God in its moving enters into it, then it looks upon the forming of the* WONDER-DOING NAME; *it sees and hears what God speaks in it; not in image-like speaking, but power-filled or vital in the understanding, as the prophets have spoken. And yet this is incomprehensible to outward reason. Of which St. Paul says, Our conversation is in heaven, Philip. 3:20, and yet also that a thorn was given him in the flesh, a messenger of Satan, (namely an opening or efflux from the spirit of lust,) to buffet him, 2 Cor. 12:7.*

*(21.) Understand this matter rightly, thus: a man sees such secret mysteries in the Spirit of Christ, in which all treasures of wisdom lie, as the Scripture testifies throughout. Thus are we to understand what the eternal counsel of God is, and then also how man may come to such vision or contemplation. We have here only hinted at the possibility, but the way or process of how to attain to it is described largely enough elsewhere.*

Thus much, we say, by way of suggestion, or in elucidation of the manner—summary yet sufficiently explicit,* in which the Questions may be treated by the Candidate, as observed on p. 663, by way of testing his own theosophic apprehensibility, along with the other specified qualifications necessary to present a just and adequate portraiture of Mr. Law’s mental constitution. We have now finally completed the task we set for ourselves in this work, and we submit the whole for the consideration of the qualified reader. Since its design and purpose have been repeatedly expressed within these pages, it is unnecessary for us to add anything further on those points at this time. What we wish to achieve is the portrait of an *ideal* man of sterling sense and genius, of solid and sufficient learning, a Christian gentleman, a sage, and a divine philosopher—in the highest sense of those terms—drawn, as it were, from a living model. We believe we have furnished such a model, or at least the materials for it, in this volume; any deficiencies may be supplied from the resources at our command, combined with the skill of the intended artist. Our object is, in effect, to establish (as a guide for the education of future generations) a practical STANDARD of a perfectly balanced or well-proportioned, uniform or <term>non-idiocratic</term> <note>not characterized by individual peculiarities or eccentricities; balanced</note>, equally developed and exactly balanced mind. This results in sound judgment regarding moral sentiment, learning, literature, science, philosophy, and Christianity—the latter* in its full <term>theosophical</term> <note>relating to a system of speculative religious philosophy which focuses on the direct knowledge of God</note> scope, as well as simple evangelical knowledge and experience.

Because he concentrates these qualifications and perfections in one character, we soberly believe we are justified in presenting the as-yet-unknown WILLIAM LAW to public notice in this regard; at the very least, he is the nearest approximation to such an estimable and admirable combination of excellence that we have ever encountered, whether in the annals of history (see Note, p. 334, 371, *etc.*) or in our own observations of life. And since his mind was, as we say, so precisely composed and arranged—by nature and by art, by true learning and piety—he applied his knowledge and judgment with equal adequacy and moral value to whatever subject he contemplated. Whether expressed through his pen or his speech, everything was, so to speak, poised and governed by perfect common sense acting under the light of high wisdom. We do not mean to say that Mr. Law was a totally regenerate or a perfect man, but only that his mind was most admirably qualified for and highly advanced in growth toward that blissful completion. The piercing, fiery sharpness, acidity, and bitterness of his natural qualities (which, like the finest fruits of this world or Paradise itself, provide the basis for a rich taste and fine spirit when perfectly mature) were not yet so perfectly influenced by the external action and internal development of the divine light that they were absolutely transformed—though they were so in his will—into paradisiacal virtues and divine graces, which constitutes perfect inward regeneration. Therefore, when he deemed it necessary, these qualities could be felt in their basic astringency and stinging sharpness by those who, when affected by them, lacked enough divine virtue to transform that action into love, or in whom such qualities of the dark principle predomi—

...nated, and who, by the evil motion of which, and its consequent harmful effect on public happiness, had given him cause, as a guardian sage of truth, to correct or reprove them.

Since this is our belief (however rhapsodic our statements may appear to those who are ignorant of how well-grounded they are, who have not *tasted* the refined intellectual food and refreshments, or *felt* and enjoyed the supreme, ravishing light that enables us to speak this way; and whose opinions and judgment on the matter, until they can speak from experience, must necessarily be fantastical and presumptuous themselves, however they may present them in an assumed guise of ability and knowledge, or a religious sentimentality of expression)—since this is, we say, our conviction (and how much our judgment deserves attention, in the absence of positive knowledge, must be either admitted or left for those capable of it to declare), we may not only be excused for our high admiration of such elevated and surpassing excellence as we have described, but even be deemed worthy of honor for having made it known to the world in this way. We have attempted by this to achieve the *object* which we state we had, and have, in view to accomplish through the present publication.

And although we have not, through this work and the several serial treatises we are preparing to accompany it (under the title of **AN INTRODUCTION TO THEOSOPHY AND MAGIA, OR THE SCIENCE OF CHRISTIANITY; Forming a STANDARD GUIDE and PRACTICAL ENTRANCE into the Mystery of NATURE, and the Arcana of its CENTRAL POWERS; the ANGELIC KNOWLEDGE of the MAGIA and CABALA of WONDER-WORKING NAMES; and the DIVINE ART of the PREPARATION of the PHILOSOPHER'S STONE, OR UNIVERSAL TINCTURE; By which to Read and Understand the Wisdom and Virtues of GOD, encoded and touched upon in the Words, Letters, and Signatures of the Book of CREATION, and to Release and Direct the Birth of the Holy Proceeding in all Things**, etc.); although we have not, we say, thereby literally met the presumed form of the terms of the following announcement of a Prize Essay, we have in effect completed the task. We doubt not it is much beyond the scope and views—though not the wishes—of the gentleman who originally proposed the theme and piously bequeathed the legacy for the purpose mentioned therein.

### THEOLOGICAL PREMIUMS.

**THEOLOGICAL PREMIUMS.**—A deceased gentleman left by his Deed of Settlement a considerable fund to be applied by his trustees, at intervals of 40 years from 1774, for the payment of TWO PREMIUMS for the best TREATISE on the following subject:—

The evidence that there is a Being—all-powerful, wise, and good—by whom everything exists; and particularly to overcome difficulties regarding the wisdom and goodness of the Deity. And this, in the first place, from considerations independent of written revelation; and in the second place, from the revelation of the Lord Jesus; and from the whole, to point out the inferences most necessary and useful to mankind.

### ADVERTISEMENT.

<margin>See the end of the Introduction to Theosophy</margin>
Notices having been given at intervals throughout this work of a proposal to publish by subscription a beautiful, new, and carefully revised edition of the theosophical works of Law, Behmen, and Freher, with their symbols, diagrams, and other illustrative drawings—which would occupy some twenty handsome octavo volumes of about 500 pages each—gentlemen and ladies who may be desirous to share in such a philanthropic enterprise, by advancing £50 or £100 each toward the expense, or by becoming subscribers for five or ten copies of the same (the total cost averaging, it is estimated, about 10s. 6d. a volume), are respectfully requested to communicate such agreement to PHILO-TEUTONICUS, as previously directed, at 24, LUDGATE STREET, LONDON. The scope and true nature of these serial writings is, in a word, the revelation and demonstration of the mystery of GOD and Nature, of eternity and time, angels and Man, and all creatures, and the reasons for things—or, in a word, the entire philosophy of Truth. We may just add that the German edition of *Böhme’s Works*, which would be strictly followed in the proposed translation, is that published in A.D. 1730, which surpasses every other for precision of arrangement as well as original correctness.

Further, we would recall to the reader’s mind what we have said respecting the necessity of a *Theosophic College*—in regard to the true, enlightened understanding of Christianity and the establishment of a system of training right subjects for its propagation in the high <term>arcana</term>, science, arts, and prerogatives of the <term>regeneration</term>—on pages 559 and 638–40 above, and elsewhere throughout this work. From the first of these references, we make the following extract:

> "May the Lord infuse into the heart of some wealthy reader of this treatise so great a power of *His love*, and kindle within it so intense and moving a desire to proclaim the Divine glory—by promoting the reign of heavenly Wisdom on earth—as shall lead to the cheerful offering of the necessary financial means for the establishment of such a scheme. For surely a more glorious, philanthropic, and sublime Christian work—one more conducive to the happiness of the world and the elevation of the human intellect—could hardly be accomplished."

One of the very appropriate employments of the chief residents there might indeed be the preparation of the above proposed new series of theosophical and other corresponding literature, presenting, in fact, an entirely new, original, and complete—and as such, standard—philosophy to the world for all future ages. In short, it would include all the science and art, theoretical and practical, for the *perfect evangelical <term>regeneration</term>*.

-># POSTSCRIPT TO THE ADVERTISEMENT.<-

The *INTRODUCTION TO THEOSOPHY*, mentioned on page 676, in 18mo format, might itself serve to present an abridged edition of the *Works of Law, Böhme, and Freher* to the English public. For instance, the Second Volume (the First Volume being almost completed) might contain Mr. Law’s ‘*Appeal*’ and ‘*Spirit of Prayer*,’ adding to the last Dialogue of this latter work the first Dialogue of the ‘*Way to Divine Knowledge*’; this would serve as a complete finish to this volume. The Third Volume might consist of the Second and Third Dialogues of the ‘*Way to Divine Knowledge*,’ removing, however, a few pages of outdated material at the beginning of the former of the Dialogues. Following this in the same Volume, the ‘*Spirit of Love*’ might be given, along with a select few of his *Letters*. The Fourth Volume might commence with Böhme’s writings, placing the *Mysterium Magnum* as the introduction to their scope and contents. And so on to the end of them, which in total might occupy eight or nine Volumes, as in the German edition. Around the Fourteenth Volume, Freher’s writings might then commence.

Next after these might be presented three or four treatises on *Animal Magnetism*, explaining its various recorded and known phenomena in a proper classification—pertaining to both body and mind, and also in respect to the instinctive and inanimate creation. These would then indicate the ground and mystery of the same, with suggestions as to its further application, all according to the established principles, properties, and laws of nature, as described in the previously given theosophical treatises. They would also show how this wonderful but as-yet undeveloped—no, misunderstood—discovery of these last ages (of vital magnetism) has always been the great *experimental requirement* for theosophy. It was alluded to and prophesied by its great masters in their writings (composing the former portion of this course of study) as an event that would assuredly arrive and should be continually expected. At that time, indeed, the writings of Böhme—or rather the realities of wisdom and truth so wonderfully structured in them—should be rendered understandable to any and every right *subject and artist*; indeed, when greater wonders of pure natural and evangelical truth (not of *Swedenborgian or other astral phantasms*) than those should be opened to contemplation and research at the will and direction of the controlling and properly trained magus. <note>See, for instance, Böhme’s allusions to the *time of lilies and roses* (the paradisiacal flowering and fruitfulness of the varieties of human life and intellect), the *downfall of Babel*, and his continual hints to his fellow students concerning the secret science and art of magic, the point of motion in nature, the *separator and tincture*, the *working creating word*, etc.; also Freher’s allusions and assurances of the same nature, as on p. 468 above; also Law’s similar assertions, as at the head of the note on p. 560 above, in his published ‘*Letters*,’ and at the end of his ‘*Animadversions on Trapp*.’</note> By the supply, then, of this compatible experimental (*à posteriori*) philosophy, and by joining it with the previously revealed (*à priori*) central philosophy of God and Nature—or as it is more properly termed, theosophy; and by coupling with it also the high Bramwell-like or *standard* evangelical and other sublime experiences of the divine life possessed by the Christian church, as implied in the contents of pages 634 to 641—by these, we say, a *key* is presented to us. Through this key, we may unlock the door and enter into, and freely explore, the most secret secrets of the practical mysteries of divine and natural magic. By this means, indeed, all that is well-grounded in the ancient Hermetic or Alchemic philosophy may be proved—if not found to be merely rudimentary concepts and powers in respect to our new, *perfected* evangelical dispensation, or the autumnal ripening in man of divine understanding and power.

The chief practical purpose, then, of these last proposed volumes in this series would be the careful explanation of the art by which humanity, regarding its moral or divine capacity, may be magically freed from its disorder, pollution, and deadness (as implied in the imperative requirements of our Lord in order to realize his life, salvation, and redemption). It would then be powerfully introduced into the birth, element, and qualifications of the *spirit of love*, or its original and redeemed inward perfection. This, it is admitted, is the goal of common Christianity; but since the latter no longer possesses the *power of the keys*, or a high degree of divine experience and hidden science, we maintain it is unable to achieve this goal as contemplated in the Gospel—which suggests that the true disciple or perfect believer in Christ shall be in-

The following, then, is a correct account of FREHER’S WRITINGS, in the order in which they were composed. After this statement, we shall present our annotations regarding the editions to be followed in case of their publication. The Titles and Contents are as follows:

(1.) SERIAL ELUCIDATIONS of the PRINCIPLES of PHILOSOPHY and THEOLOGY of BÖHME, surnamed the TEUTONIC THEOSOPHER. In NINE VOLUMES.

VOL. A.—(1.) Of GOD considered APART FROM ALL NATURE and CREATION. (2.) Of GOD, considered as MANIFESTING HIMSELF through Eternal NATURE. Of the TWO CO-ETERNAL PRINCIPLES—Of the SEVEN PROPERTIES—And of the THREE CONSTITUENT PARTS of NATURE. With a SYMBOL in illustration of the subject.

VOL. B.—AN EXPLANATION of that SCHEME, or Table of BÖHME, wherein GOD is CONSIDERED in UNITY and TRINITY, APART FROM ALL NATURE and CREATION.—(3.) AN ANSWER to an OBJECTION concerning the DESIRE’S ATTRACTION of ITSELF.—(4.) Of the FURTHER, MORE EXTERNAL MANIFESTATION of GOD through the CREATION of ANGELS. Of MATERIAL CAUSES.—(5.) Of the FALL of LUCIFER and ALL his ANGELS.

VOL. C.—(6.) Of the CREATION of this, our OUTWARD THIRD PRINCIPLE, in which we Live, Move, and have our Outward Being. With a DISCOURSE on the SCOPE of ST. JOHN’S WORDS, ‘IN THE BEGINNING.’

VOL. D.—(7.) Of the FALL of MAN from his primeval GLORY and PERFECTION down INTO the SPIRIT of THIS WORLD.—(8.) Of the NATURAL PROPAGATION of MAN in this now CURSED four-element WORLD.—(9.) Of MAN’S REGENERATION through the BLOOD and DEATH of CHRIST.

VOL. E.—(10.) Of the ETERNAL WORD BECOMING FLESH. Or of the PURE, IMMACULATE CONCEPTION and INCARNATION of our LORD JESUS CHRIST in the WOMB of the blessed VIRGIN MARY.

The author made considerable enlargements in the ‘Explanation’ of the First Table; and in the year 1727, an alteration was made in the Second and Third Tables by the substitution of a *Peacock* for a *Hunting Dog*, according to J. B.’s metaphor in his ‘Mysterium Magnum,’ xxi. 12. We shall, therefore, present this work as if it were composed in A.D. 1717.

<note>The preceding treatises clarifying the scope and principles of the philosophy and theology of BOHEMIUS were written at the request of esteemed friends of the author and lent to them for reading; among these friends may be mentioned the learned Francis Lee and the Rev. E. Waple of St. Sepulchre’s, Skinner Street. Indeed, it would appear from observations shared by the author throughout his writings that everything he undertook of this nature up to the year 1712 was done entirely at the entreaties of his friends on specific occasions. Around the close of the seventeenth and the early part of the eighteenth century, the writings of Bohemius (those that could be obtained, for they were then as rare to find as they are now) were earnestly studied by many learned persons; some of whom (as might well be imagined) formed misconceptions of their very profound yet exact and true sense, and so raised objections to such points and claims in them as seemed to them in disagreement with sound philosophy. Among the latter parties, it appears, was one Mr. P., a friend of the Rev. Mr. Waple mentioned above, who therefore requested our author to clear up the true sense of J. B.’s foundation, which had seemed uncertain to his friend; whereupon he wrote the following Treatise, as on similar occasions, the remaining pieces of this series. These latter, we suspect, were composed between the years 1705 and 1712.</note>

**VOL. F.—NOTHING AND SOMETHING.** Being a DISCOURSE concerning the TRUE SIGNIFICANT SENSE of BOHEMIUS’S DEEPEST, ETERNAL, or ABYSSAL NOTHING. HOW this NOTHING (according to his Gift and Declaration) BRINGS ITSELF FORTH INTO SOMETHING, in and through the PROCESS of Eternal NATURE. HOW this SOMETHING is DISTINGUISHED FROM (or WHETHER, and in WHAT SENSE it may be called OPPOSITE TO) that former NOTHING. BUT more especially, HOW ALL HIS different DESCRIPTIONS of the DIVINE BEING, in UNITY and TRINITY—now as BEFORE or WITHOUT, and then as IN or AFTER Eternal NATURE (only by means of UNDERSTANDING distinctly the PROPER MEANING of his ETERNAL NOTHING and SOMETHING)—may be found standing, without any Contradiction, in a MOST HARMONIOUS CONCORDANCE. Written in EXPLICATION of FOUR EMBLEMATIC FIGURES, in which what is stated here in Words is represented by several Signs and Characters for a more distinct understanding.

**NOTE.—**The Four emblematic Figures mentioned in this title (or as they might have been very properly termed—a Four-fold spiritual Figure) constitute the first four of the ‘Thirteen Theosophic Emblems’ which were later engraved and inserted at the end of the Second Volume of J. B.’s Works, large 4to., published A.D. 1764. These four Figures, containing the basis of divine revelation, the author enlarged into the Scheme in question around the year 1710, we judge. They were, probably, composed to clarify the single Symbol invented and inserted by the author at the end of VOL. A, *above*, which figure might not have been clear to the readers of that discourse; whereupon, on further reflection, the author was enabled to present his conception in this more lucid and successful manner. Question: Were the four circularly enclosed figures on page 4 of our 4to. collection of fair copies of all the Author’s symbolic illustrations to his writings also originally intended for, or belonging to, this figure at the end of VOL. A, or to the treatise in question? These are respectively headed: *Without all Nature—An Eternal Nothing—Why the Eternal Nothing introduces itself into Nature and Creature—And, How the Eternal Nothing introduces itself into Nature?* We think whether so or not, in case of publication they should go with the latter. <note>This treatise was not finished because the objector admitted he was mistaken and was satisfied by what the author had so far given. The first nine pieces of the next following Volume (G.), however, supply what is missing from it.</note>

**VOL. G** —(1.) NINETY-SEVEN POSITIONS concerning GOD in UNITY and TRINITY, CONSIDERED BOTH BEFORE and AFTER Eternal NATURE, according to BOHEMIUS’S CENTRAL PHILOSOPHY.—(2.) GENERAL POSITIONS concerning the DIVINE BEING in UNITY and TRINITY, and especially the GENERATION of ETERNAL NATURE, gathered from our FORMER WRITINGS, according to the mind of BOHEMIUS, and all taken either immediately FROM HIS own plain, unquestionable WORDS, or by means of an EVIDENT CONSEQUENCE flowing forth freely out of them. *An unfinished treatise.* <note>At the end of some thirty pages of this Discourse, we find the following remark made by the author: *Here the matter was interrupted, nay, broken off with violence.*</note>—(3.) HOW the PROPERTIES of Eternal NATURE are to be considered IN GOD.—(4.) HOW the TWO SIMILES used in a FORMER DISCOURSE do NOT IMPLY that there are TWO TRINITIES.—(5.) FIVE QUESTIONS, raised FROM THE FORMER DISCOURSES, ANSWERED.—(6.) CONCERNING the Expression, DARKNESS in GOD.—(7.) ANSWERS to the following TWO QUESTIONS: first, *Whether Bohemius asserts that there was a motion of the central fire with its own self-desire, whereby the Will of God was stirred in both fires and the wrath-fire broke forth, before the Fall of Angels?* Second, *What is the true notion of "own self-desire" as it relates to fire and forms, and such like things that are in themselves inanimate; since "will" and "desire," in the proper sense of speech, belong only to intellectual and rational beings?*—(8.) A CONFERENCE (between A and B) concerning ETERNAL NATURE, whether it is OUT OF GOD or only EFFECTED BY HIS WILL.—(9.) REPRESENTATIONS of BOHEMIUS’S ETERNAL LIBERTY and ABYSSAL UNITY, *pari passu ambulant* <note>Latin: walking at an equal pace.</note>.

The "Discourse of NOTHING and SOMETHING" was previously mentioned. It cannot now be determined whether the author ever finished this piece or if he abandoned it with the intention of presenting its intended contents in the projected *Conferences on Predestination*. However, it is certain that the last-mentioned "CONFERENCE" fragment was left by the author in the state in which it is now found. Furthermore, there could also have been introduced here the remaining fragment in the author’s handwriting (as all these mentioned fragments are), which we have named "A THEOSOPHIC CONFESSION OF FAITH." Written in German and English side by side, it begins at PROPOSITION XCV and ends at PROPOSITION CXXIV. There is every reason to conclude that this last priceless piece was actually completed and that it was written by the author *immediately after* the treatise of the "*BECOMING MAN, etc.*" described in VOL. E, above; but no traces now exist of the earlier or later portions of it beyond those described above. To resume:

(10.) THE PROCESS OF THE PHILOSOPHICAL WORK, considered as thoroughly analogous to man's redemption through Jesus Christ, and represented by positions regarding its principal circumstances. According to the description given in Jacob Boehme’s *SIGNATURA RERUM*, Chapters vii, x, xi, xii. — (11.) THE GROWTH of VEGETABLES (with respect to their yearly renewal in the springtime) as described by <term>Bohemius</term>.

VOL. H. — CRITICAL OBSERVATIONS UPON THE REV. EDWARD WAPLE’S EXERCITATIONS UPON THE PHILOSOPHY AND THEOLOGY OF <term>BOHEMIUS</term>, as explained in the PRECEDING DISCOURSES and as set forth in Jacob Boehme’s writings, made at Waple's own request.

VOL. I. — The DETAILED CONTENTS of all the former treatises (*see pages* 461—91 *above*). [The above series of writings were composed, as we have stated, between A.D. 1699 and 1712, when Mr. Waple died; at which time, it would appear, our author lived in his house.]

### (2.) HIEROGLYPHICA SACRA, or DIVINE EMBLEMS, IN THIRTEEN FIGURES, with their EXPLANATIONS. In explanation of the birth and beginning of nature, and of the moral progress and end of things.

### (3.) SIXTEEN CONFERENCES, CONCERNING the modern DOCTRINE of PREDESTINATION. Illustrated with symbols and diagrams. In which the subject is fundamentally explained from the ground of nature as well as from Scripture. In eight volumes.

VOL. I. — THE FIRST CONFERENCE. An argument against investigating the doctrine of predestination. — THE SECOND CONFERENCE. Proving that the Scriptures do not always mean the exact same thing by the words "God" and "Lord." — THE THIRD CONFERENCE. Of the Deity considered as he is in himself only, *outside of nature*. Point, Centre, Circumference. — THE FOURTH CONFERENCE. Of the Deity as manifested in and through the properties of eternal nature, which are and must be seven. — THE FIFTH CONFERENCE. Concerning the three radical or inferior properties, and each of them in particular.

VOL. II. — THE SIXTH CONFERENCE. Concerning the fourth property of eternal nature, located between the three inferior and the three superior properties. With three long digressions. The first, against Socinus; the second, proving that this nature is justly called eternal; and the third, against that new (*Bourignon-Poiret*) doctrine which denies an absolute necessity for the death of Christ upon the cross. [The subject of this latter digression was made the foundation of a large special discourse, which immediately followed the present work.] — THE SEVENTH CONFERENCE. Concerning the three superior properties of eternal nature. The production of the fourth property, or united power of fire and light. A parable of *All-mine* etc. God, and our God. Jacob Boehme’s word, *<term>Scientz</term>*, not correctly expressed by the English word "science." A true fable of *Will-mine*. Riches and poverty of eternity.

VOL. III. — THE EIGHTH CONFERENCE. Concerning the two co-eternal principles of nature. Of annihilation and transmutation. — THE NINTH CONFERENCE. Being a particular consideration of that noble simile so much recommended to our consideration by <term>Bohemius</term>.

<note>Up to this point, the author has only been preparing the way for a fundamental resolution of the doctrine according to the central philosophy of Bohemius. In the remaining conferences, it is settled first according to the Scripture, and then according to the previously opened ground of nature, being represented according to Jacob Boehme’s deep and full sense of it. The chief importance of this work consists in the comprehensive and clear explanation of the *seven properties of nature*, with its two co-eternal principles and three constituent parts (darkness, fire, and light), which is contained in the third to the ninth conferences described above. This most essential knowledge of the seven properties of nature is not so clearly, copiously, and demonstratively exhibited in any other of this author’s works as in the present treatises. No one can have any legitimate claim to a knowledge of theosophical truth until he has mastered, in understanding and experience, this most fundamental subject of the constituent ground of nature.</note>

VOL. IV. — THE TENTH CONFERENCE. [In which the doctrine is settled, so far, only according to the Scripture.] Predestination explained through seven details in the simile of a wise man. Five kinds of predestination excluded from this discourse. Proofs that God neglected no soul, neither before, nor under, nor after the Law.

VOL. V. — THE ELEVENTH CONFERENCE. Three preliminaries: first, what truth is in the Scriptures; secondly, of the letter and the spirit; and thirdly, of rightly dividing the word of truth. *<term>Voluntas Signi et Beneplaciti</term>* (The revealed and secret will of God). Of the turning of man’s will. Of God showing mercy to whom he will. Of Pharaoh hardened. Of Jacob and Esau. Of the Father’s giving men to the Son. Objections raised from Romans 9 and other places in Scripture. Of St. Paul and St. James regarding justification.

VOL. VI. — THE TWELFTH CONFERENCE. St. Paul and St. James reconciled regarding justification. The strongest predestinarian argument answered. A dream about the doctor. Of Pharaoh again, as well as of Jacob and Esau. Election and reprobation are not two parallel branches of predestination.
