## BOOK VII.—THE SPIRIT OF LOVE, OR THE FULL BIRTH, END, TRUTH, AND LIFE OF REGENERATION. IN THREE PARTS.—Being an Answer to Two Objections against the Doctrine of the former Discourses, which represents the Deity as pure Love.

The objections are expressed as follows. First, that the doctrine of *pure and universal love* may be too refined and imaginary; because (says the objector), "I find that however much I like it, I cannot attain it or overcome all that in my nature which is contrary to it, no matter what I do; and so I am only able to be an admirer of that love which I cannot grasp." Second, because I find so much said in Scripture of a righteousness and justice, a wrath and vengeance of God that must be atoned for and satisfied, etc.; though I am in love with the description of the Deity given in these discourses as a being who is all love, yet I have some doubt whether Scripture will allow it. These are the objections; the answers to them occupy the first and second parts of the present treatise, respectively. The third part is a practical evangelical application of the subject and a conclusion to all the preceding discourses.

### PART FIRST. Answer to the First Objection: which is contained in a *Letter from Theophilus to Theogenes*.—

The nature and perfection of the *spirit of love*. No man can participate in this spirit until he lives freely, willingly, and universally according to it. Its indispensable necessity as the means of union between God and man. The state of nature and of man as deprived of the spirit of love by reason of the Fall. The process of its recovery by *purification*. The fundamental reason for this process, explained in a description of *Nature and its seven properties*. The similarity of these properties in the nature and being of man. All evil is the consequence of nature working in *self*, or in a state of separation from God. All good is the power and presence of the supernatural Deity, dwelling and working in the properties of Nature. How His presence and the birth of the spirit of love are the same thing. Being a *spirit of life*, it can arise in only one way and from only one cause. Its *birth* by the *kindling of the eternal fire, or the opening of the supernatural light in the center of (nature in) the soul*, and the consequent transformation of the soul's natural life. Hence the truth and necessity of Christian redemption and the doctrine of the *Cross*.

### PART SECOND. Answer to the Second Objection. This is set forth in *Two Dialogues between Theophilus and Theogenes, accompanied by a Friend*.

*Dialogue I.*—The Deity, an infinite source of pure overflowing love and joy. All nature and every creature brought forth to manifest and rejoice in this divine love and happiness. Nothing can be in God which is not infinite and eternal. What wrath is in itself. It can be nowhere but in nature, and then only in a state of disorder. The origin of wrath and evil is the same. In man, it occurs at the disunion of his twofold life—of Deity and nature. All man's salvation and good comes from the manifestation of the life of the Deity in the soul. Perpetual inspiration is essential to a life of goodness. The ground of salvation is the *inspoken word* of the divine nature. This is the subject of all revealed dispensations. The earthly self is to be resisted and renounced. Wrath is ascribed to God because the creature has changed its state in nature and therefore must experience God as He is manifested in the working of nature. How wrath originates in nature, though nature is a manifestation of the Deity. God and nature are distinguished. Wrath is kindled by the will of the creature when it breaks or loses the union of the seven heavenly properties. The Deity is a supernatural governing love and wisdom, always seeking the restoration of fallen nature and creatures. The texts of Scripture confine the working of wrath to the powers of nature. Vengeance is not allowed to man because that is working with fallen nature. It belongs only to God, who is supernatural—that is, to the light and love of God.

*Dialogue II.*—The atonement for the Divine wrath or justice, and the extinguishing of sin in the creature, are only different expressions for one and the same thing. The analogy of Scripture teaches this. The atonement is the single work of regeneration, when rightly understood. The sufferings and death of Christ are the gracious effects of divine love and goodness. In what sense the justice or righteousness of God is satisfied thereby. Man's original righteousness from God was his law. No peace until this is perfectly restored or satisfied. The fact that God is all love does not abate the force of the scriptural denunciations of eternal torments (or punishments) for those who live and die in sin. The popular doctrine of the vicarious suffering of Christ is erroneous and opens a door either to superstition or to infidelity. "Christ's suffering and dying were nothing else than Christ conquering and overcoming all the false good and hellish evil of the fallen state of man. His resurrection and ascension into heaven, though great in themselves and necessary parts of our deliverance, are only the consequences and effects of his sufferings and death—his entering into possession of what he had obtained by them." The necessity and efficacy of the sufferings and death of Christ as that which qualified Him to become a common *father of life* to all who died in Adam. They were only acceptable to the love of God on that account. How we, by virtue of Christ's accomplished process, have victory over all the evils of our fallen state and shall rise to the glory of Christ—heirs of God. The Bible is to be studied in this simple, adorable light.

### PART THIRD. Of the Art of "DYING TO SELF," and of attaining to the "full birth of LOVE." Or, of the actual CONVERSION of the WILL with its Imagination and Desire, wholly and unceasingly to GOD. Being a Practical Conclusion to the preceding discourses.

*Dialogue III.*—The practical ground of the spirit of love. The moral and pleasant aspects of this natural life are easily mistaken (by mere reasoners and transcendentalists) for the spirit of divine love in the soul. The danger of this delusion. *The doctrine and the spirit of love itself are two very different things.* How we are to acquire the spirit of love. The Scripture doctrine of *election and reprobation* in its fundamental basis. The figures under which it is represented: *Cain* and *Abel*, *Esau* and *Jacob*, *etc.* Nothing is elected but the "seed" of the new man, or the heavenly birth within us; all else

What divine love is, and its effects within us. All that we are and have from Adam as fallen—all must be given up, if the *birth of divine love* is to be brought forth in us. All our natural contrariety to divine love must be lost and swallowed up in it, as darkness is unperceived in the light. This was the state of the first man, previous to the fall.—Concerning darkness and light. The priority and glory of Light; which is ALL POWER. In itself invisible and incomprehensible, and only known by possessing darkness, or substantiality. Light is immaterial, though materiality is always present with visible light. All light, whether in heaven or earth, is only so much darkness illuminated. All nature and creature as such are darkness; and therefore can only work according to the *powers of darkness*. Nothing is evil or tormenting but that which nature or *self* does. *Self* or nature is the three properties of desire thrown into a fourth of wrath, through the loss or unattainability of their only (supernatural) good. No possible deliverance from *self* but by the new birth of the supernatural Deity in the soul. Desire is the ground of life, and all sensibility of life. How this is manifest in outward nature, by attraction, with its essential properties. The relations of the visible world and all its productions to the invisible and hellish world. The way of escaping from, and abolishing all evil arising in the soul, or the art of *dying to self*. God must be and do all: the state of heart that the perfect conviction of this truth induces. The results of a true practical conformity to this conviction, or the *spirit of prayer*. The *marriage-feast* of the soul and Virgin SOPHIA, or the full birth of the spirit of *love*. The one simple way to attain this, as shown here, is the one infallible way, because the will is the leader of the creaturely life. Christ, having obtained an infinite power over the human nature, must sooner or later see all enemies under his feet. Summary conclusion.

# BÖHME’S WRITINGS. (*Intro. to Theos. iv—xv., roy. 18mo., 4to.*)

A SUMMARY Account of the Works of JACOB BÖHME, wherein is revealed the mystery of the supernatural DEITY and VIRGIN WISDOM, and of the birth and ground of NATURE; the creation of angels, and the fall of one hierarchy of them; the creation of this gross, mutable world, or temporary principle of nature; and the ground and development, or the entire mystery of MAN (as ADAM and CHRIST, composing every individual) in his creation, in the process of his fall, and in the process of his restoration or cure. Also, with respect to his individual process of regeneration and his ultimate deification.

[☞ The emblem at the head of Böhme’s works is an angel passing through the air, blowing a trumpet, signifying the demonstration of the Gospel religion by a revelation of *universal and self-evident truth*; out of which these words sound forth:—*To all Christians, Jews, Turks, and Heathens, to all the nations of the earth, this trumpet sounds for the last time.*]

<margin>VOL. IV. (*bourgeois*.)</margin>
1. *Aurora. The Dawning of the Eternal Day, or the Infancy of Creation.—An unfinished piece*, of the childhood of his illumination. [Wherein he describes as best he could—as a stammering, timid, unlettered child—the opening panorama of the divine wisdom set before his internal vision. He narrates the circumstances and ground of the angelic creation; the fall of the chief of the three hierarchies of it, and the direful effects which ensued thereafter in eternal nature (by their unbalancing of its seven equipoised powers or forces); and the subsequent creation of this material, temporal system (from the condensed, compacted, dark, fiery, fluidic, spoiled materiality and galvanic powers of the spiritual, angelic world, good as well as bad) as the first act of the curative process of the *evil* thus originated in nature. The narrative was broken off by violence before the author reached the creation of Man.—This piece *should not be perused* until the reader is fairly conversant with J. B.’s other works; as his descriptions here of the *seven spirits*, by reason of his lack of understanding at the time regarding the origin of the fourth property, the *fire*, differ from and are relatively inferior to those contained in the subsequent treatises, where *that point* had become recognized in his understanding. This fourth property is the opening of the life of the supernatural liberty, abyssal nothingness, or free magic eye—in nature; that is, of the pure Deity in nature.] A.D. 1612.

2. *De Tribus Principiis cum Appendice*. Of the Three Principles or Worlds of Nature, with Appendix.—Describing the eternal birth of nature in its seven properties and two co-eternal principles, as well as this third principle and the creation of all things. Lastly of MAN, as the crown and comprehension, or developed central divine idea of all, and therefore a true lord and prince over all. His fall, with all its circumstances, and his redemption by virtue of the ‘mystery’ and process of Christ. With a concurrent evangelical application of the truths developed. A.D. 1618.—[Herein man’s creation is declared, from which it appears that man is the noblest being in the universe of God. That he is the primal center, the immediate abode, habitation, organism, and personal medium of Deity, who, as the triune, incomprehensible, universal power or Spirit of life—a mere goodness, light, and truth—has no form nor visibility except in man—understand the VIRGIN man as created, and as restored and glorified in Christ. (OH, MAN! SEEK AND KNOW THYSELF.)—In this work, man (who was created as the instrument by which God would heal the disordered, corrupted *body* of nature and restore all to its primitive perfection) is circumstantially described in his original creation, his fall, and his redemption by the “*mystery of Christ;*” who, as a second Adam or man, came to heal and restore the first ruined Adam, and to effect all that which

<margin>VI.</margin>
3. *De Triplici Vita Hominis.* Of the Threefold Life of Man, according to the Three Principles. That is, as the generated Idea, or Supernatural Image of the *abyssal* triune Will-spirit of the Deity—the VIRGIN SOPHIA, incarnated in and clothed with Eternal and Temporal Nature. Based on the relations of Man’s present state of grace and nature, it sets forth his practical duties and obligations for regeneration and the attainment of the prerogatives of his glorious redemption in Christ. A.D. 1619.

<margin>VII.</margin>
4. *Psychologia Vera cum Supplemento.* Forty Questions concerning the Soul of Man, Answered, with a Supplement. In the answer to the First Question, a symbolical diagram is presented of the Wonder-Eye of Divine Wisdom, the supernatural Abyss or Habitation of the Triune Deity. It includes the Central Generation within it (by the Father-Will of the Trinity of the Deity) of Eternal Nature, with its two co-eternal principles of black Darkness and lustrous Light, and this ex-generated third or mixed temporal principle understood within them. A.D. 1620. <note>Understand these two eternal principles of the *negative* and the *positive*, the *no* and the *yes* of the speaking triune Word of Life, the SUPREME ONE—that they together constitute Nature, or eternal Nature: not the dark world alone, which is termed the ground or root of nature, but both principles together, in *perfect, indissoluble union.* By the fall of angels (through the perverse, obstinate, proud, self-willed, ignorant, and rebellious misuse of their free, uncontrollable will; being unduly elevated by the sudden perception of their own wonderful beauty, power, and glory) who had their life and being, or *qualification*, in this eternal or divine nature—it was discovered or experienced how the majestic *visibility*, body, or "glory of God," or "kingdom of heaven," has this darkness as its basis or ground. It was also seen how the *severed* life of this dark principle *in itself* is a life of the most horrible wrath, anguish, falsehood, and misery. And hence arose the Scripture and theological term, *God’s wrath*, or the *wrath of God*—signifying, not that the will-spirit of the Deity is wrathful or capable of wrath, for He is the only good, pure, and lovely one, the unchangeable love; but that in bringing forth His ineffable, intellectual, will-spirit into a perceptible essence or nature—something sensible to creatures by *desire*—this desire, as such, must be the *very opposite* or contrary spirit to His own Being of gentleness, peace, delight, holiness, and happiness. By overcoming or possessing this contrary spirit, His real goodness, holiness, light, and truth become manifested in a triumphant, glorious life. *This* twofold life is then Nature: eternal Nature, the "divine nature" in which all immortal beings are created to live and enjoy divine happiness. Yet alas, how many frustrate the divine intention and render ineffectual the divine benevolence toward them in the incarnation, sufferings, and death of Christ; and so they fall into the dark, fiery center, self-contracting generation, or root of Nature—*the eternal dying of the divine liberty, the life of desire, wrath, and all misery.*</note>

<margin>VIII.</margin>
5. *De Incarnatione Verbi, Three Parts.*—Part One. Of the Incarnation of Jesus Christ the Son of God. That is, concerning the *Virgin* Mary: what she was from the beginning, and what kind of mother she became through the *Blessing* and conception of her Son, Jesus Christ; and how the Eternal Word has become Man.—Part Two. Of the Suffering, Dying, Death, Resurrection, Ascension, and Glorification of Christ, as the first and second Adam. And why we must all *follow Him* in the same process and way now opened for us, back to the Throne of God.—Part Three. Of the Tree of the Christian Faith; showing the whole Christian doctrine of faith and practice. Entirely brought forth out of the Supernatural Centre, through the Three Principles. A.D. 1620.

<margin>VIII.*</margin>
6. *Sex Puncta Theosophica.* Containing a description of the life of the Supernatural Wisdom and Abyss of Deity, and of the Three Principles of Nature, as well as each principle in itself. Showing how people should seek, find, and know the Ground of Nature.—7. *Sex Puncta Mystica.* Clarifying certain deep points involved but not resolved in the previous dissertations.—8. *Mysterium Pansophicum.* A further, diversified, and deep consideration concerning the heavenly and earthly mystery of nature, and of the full working and enjoyment of the life of the latter. A.D. 1620.

<margin>IX.</margin>
9. *De Signatura Rerum.* Showing the sense, virtue, and quality of the shapes and forms of creation. It explains what the beginning, ruin, and cure of everything is, both spiritual and physical. <note>The basis of Physiognomy, Phrenology, Homeopathy, etc. The Language of Nature, or Speech of Divine Wisdom, understandable by her regenerate, clairvoyant children. A book of the sublimest wisdom and angelic melody, and a key to the regeneration of the medical art.</note> A.D. 1621.

Or, of continual dying to self, and immersing the will and desire wholly into the meekness, humility, and love of the supernatural, divine element.—13. *De Tentatione, and 4 Com-*

> * I beg leave respectfully to observe that it would have been well if the recent Synod held at Rome had condescended to look into this author's demonstration and revelation of the "mystery of Christ" before issuing to the world the *false dogma (!)* it recently proposed regarding the immaculate conception of the Blessed Virgin Mary. Her high blessedness and inward reconstitution—by which she became interiorly as highly elevated as Adam when he was breathed forth from the womb of Deity, and nothing could be higher (thus qualifying her to be the mother of the throne-prince of eternity, the "man Christ Jesus"—God and man)—took place only upon her acceptance of the divine salutation through the angel Gabriel. The loan of a copy of this *Book of the Incarnation* was offered to the Synod during its sessions by the writer, through the agency of the See of Rome in this county, but it was not accepted, or the offer was overlooked, although it was acknowledged. *January, 1856.*

Complexions. Of the Ground and Nature of Temptation; from where it arises, and how to overcome in the conflict. [The first three tracts composed the only book the author published in print: all the rest of his writings were left by him in the hands of his friends, in manuscript.] A.D. 1622. IX,

14. ***Libri Apologetici duo, contra Balth. Tilken.*** Two Apologies.—The first, in defense and elucidation of the *Aurora*. The second, concerning Predestination; and of the Person of Christ, and the Virgin Mary, as treated in the previously named *Book of the Incarnation*. A.D. 1621, 23.—

15. ***Anti Stiefelius, libri duo.*** (1.) Considerations of E. S.'s book, concerning the Threefold State of Man, and the New Birth; also of the Last Zion, or New Jerusalem, etc. (2.) Concerning the errors of the sects of E. S. and Ezechiel Meth relating to Christian Perfection. A.D. 1621, 22.—

16. ***Apologia contra G. Richter, cum libello Apologetico ad Senatum Gærlicensem.*** The Author's defense of his printed book *The Way to Christ*, and his *Aurora*, against the libellous censures of the Primate, G. Richter. A.D. 1624. X.

17. ***De Electione Gratiæ, cum Appendice de Pœnitentia.*** Being a fundamental demonstration of the Scripture doctrine of Election, or Predestination. With an Appendix, showing the way to attain to the clear vision and knowledge of Divine Mysteries. A.D. 1623. [Grounded in the deepest supernatural, abyssal center—the instinct, constitution, or *scientz* of the Fountain Word and Creator of all things; and from there traced into and through Nature. And showing the inevitability of that which is evil and that which is good.] XI.

18. ***Mysterium Magnum:*** an Exposition of the First Book of Moses, called Genesis. In three parts. In which is treated the revelation of the Divine Word, through the Three Principles of Nature; and of the origin of the world and the creation. Also, in which the Kingdom of Nature and the Kingdom of Grace are explained. A.D. 1623. [Demonstrating the literal truth of the descriptions in the book of Genesis. But to understand such truth, a magic understanding is necessary; one versed in theosophical science, and also in the modern experimentalism of animal magnetism, clairvoyance, spiritism, mediumship, etc. That is, the incidents narrated being penned from a central vision—of the two eternal principles and of time—therefore only a similarly regenerated, divine understanding can properly grasp the true and full sense of it.] XII, XIII.

*Christosophia. Second Part.*—19. ***Theoscopia.*** Of Divine Contemplation: how to attain divine clairvoyance and understanding, or wisdom. (Unfinished.)—20. ***De Vita Mentali.*** Of the Supersensual, Super-rational, or Divine Intellectual Life. [See *F. Lee's* enlargement of this piece in Vol. IV., large 4to., English edition of *J. B.'s* Works; which is the most preferable.]—21. ***Colloquium Viatorum.*** A dialogue between a regenerated soul and one who is in the way or process, seeking the full birth of Divine Wisdom.—22. ***Epitome de Mysterio Magno.*** A theosophic summary of the grounds and process of regeneration.—23. ***Appendix. Suspiria Viatorum.*** The Holy Prayer Book (containing prayers of the highest magnetic power and virtue). Left unfinished. A.D. 1624. XIV.

24. ***De Testamento Christi.*** Of Baptism and the Supper. How they are to be understood, according to both the Old and New Testaments. Set forth from the true theosophical ground, through the Three Principles of the Divine Manifestation. A.D. 1624. XIII.

25. ***Quæstiones Theosophicæ.*** Being a consideration of the Divine Revelation. That is, of God, Nature, and Creation, Heaven, Hell, and this world, together with all creatures. From where all things in nature have their origin, for what purpose, and why they are created. Especially of MAN, or *Adam and Christ*. Set forth in 177 questions, with answers to thirteen of them. (Unfinished.)—26. ***Tabula Principiorum.*** A table or consideration of the Deity, in Unity, Trinity, and Wisdom, and as manifested through the Three Principles of Nature; with the explanation of it. This table accompanies the Author's epistle 'Of the True and False Light' of understanding, dated 11 Nov. 1623.—27. ***Tabulæ Principiorum.*** Three tables of the Divine Manifestation. Showing how God is to be considered in his supernatural abyss, and as manifested in and by Nature, with its two principles and seven properties, and further by this world. And then concerning MAN as an image or epitome of all worlds, in his creation, his fall, and his redemption in Christ. Being a key to the whole of the Author's revelations.—28. ***Clavis.*** Or an explanation of some principal points and expressions in the Author's writings. [In the German edition, there is an additional *Key*, which has not yet been translated into English.] A.D. 1624. XIV.

29. ***Epistolæ Theosophicæ.*** Being a collection of the Author's letters, written during the last six years of his life, in which he composed all his theosophical treatises, except the *Aurora*. [These epistles should be read first, as an introduction to his writings.] XV.

To begin a proper study of these writings, the reader is advised to first go through the treatises of Mr. Law, contained in Volumes I, II, and III of the “*Introduction to Theosophy*,” named on pages xix and xxvi–xxix, and in the order given there.† Then, having obtained a concept of the entire scope and unity of Böhme's philosophy (starting with the supernatural ground, out of which—or rather in the center of which free, clear-seeing Eye or vision, as a point—Nature is eternally generated by the astringent motion, attraction, or self-desire of the Divine Triune Will, or Word of life, within it, and universally possessing the same), he will be well prepared to pursue his object, according to the special directions given for that end by Mr. Law to an academic friend at the end of “*The Way to Divine Knowledge*.” Freher's writings will be found to be a sequential study to the whole, and are as follows.

# FREHER’S WRITINGS. (*Intro. to Theos.*, xvi.—xlii, royal 18mo., 4to.)

A BRIEF ACCOUNT OF FREHER’S WRITINGS, being comments upon the above-described writings of the divine regenerate and clairvoyant, Böhme. They are entitled, *FUNDAMENTA MYSTICA JACOBI BOHEMII TEUTONICI, EXPLICATA. PER ANDREAM DIONYSIUM FREHERUM* <note>Mystical Foundations of Jakob Böhme the Teuton, Explained. By Andrew Dionysius Freher.</note>. (See also, *British Museum, Add. MSS.* 5767-5794.)

1. *Serial Elucidations of J. B.'s Principles of Philosophy and Theology*; in EIGHT VOLUMES, with an INDEX VOLUME. A.D. 1698—1705. Namely:
**Vol. A.** (1.) *Of Deity considered without all Nature and Creature.* (2.) *Of Deity, as Manifesting Himself by Eternal Nature; with its Seven Properties, Two Principles, and Three Distinctions or Parts.*
**Vol. B.** (§.) *An Explanation of J. B.'s Tables of* Deity outside Nature. (§.) *Answer to Objection concerning the* Desire's Attraction of Itself. (3.) *Of the further Exterior Manifestation of God, or the Divine Nature, in the Creation of Angels*, with (§.) *Answer to Objections concerning Angels and Men, 'out of God,' and Material Causes.* (4.) *Of the Fall of Lucifer and all his Angels.*
**Vol. C.** (5.) *Of the Creation of this Third or Temporal Principle of Nature, wherein we live and have our Outward Being.*
**Vol. D.** (6.) *Of the Fall of Man from his Primeval Glory, down into the Spirit and Grossness of this Astral Principle.* (7.) *Of the Natural Propagation of Man in this now Cursed, Four-elementary World.* (8.) *Of Man's Regeneration, through the Blood and Death of Christ.*
**Vol. E.** (9.) *Of the Eternal Word's becoming Flesh: Or of the Pure, Immaculate Conception and Incarnation of our Lord Jesus Christ in the Womb of the Blessed Virgin Mary.* <note>The author's references are always to the 1682 German edition of J. B.'s works.</note>—
**Vol. F.** (SECOND SERIES.) *Nothing and All, and Something. A Discourse concerning the true Sense of J. B.'s Eternal or Abyssal Nothing (and All). How this posits itself as Something, in and by the Process of Eternal Nature. And showing how J. B.'s different and contradictory Descriptions of the Deity in Unity and Trinity, as before, and then as in Eternal Nature, stand in perfect Harmonious Concordance.*
**Vol. G.** (1.) *Ninety-seven Positions concerning God in Unity and Trinity, both as Before and After Eternal Nature.* (2.) *General Positions concerning the Divine Being in Unity and Trinity, and especially the Generation of Eternal Nature.* (3.) *How the Properties of Eternal Nature are to be considered in God.* (4.) *How that the Two Similes of a Former Discourse do not imply Two Trinities.* (5.) *Five Questions, raised out of the former Discourses, Answered.* (6.) *Concerning the Expression, 'Darkness in God.'* (7.) *Answers to Two Questions.* (8.) *Concerning Eternal Nature, whether out of God, or only effected by his Will.* (9.) *Representations of J. B.'s Eternal Liberty and Abyssal Unity, walking at an equal pace.* (10.) *The Process of the Philosophical Work, by the duly prepared Magus or Artist.* (11.) *The Growing of Vegetables in their Yearly Renewing, as described by J. B.*—
**Vol. H.** *Critical Corrections of Rev. E. Waple's Exercises upon the Philosophy and Theology of J. B., as set forth in the preceding First Five Vols.*—Vol. I. *The Particular Contents of all the Former Treatises.*—Also Several Fragmentary Pieces, described in the note of p. 680 onwards.

<note>The contents of the treatises of Vols. F. and G., with those of A. and B., are of the utmost importance to be understood in order to "rightly divide the word of truth" in J. B.'s deep and diversified revelations of it.</note>

<margin>XVI—XXV.</margin>
2. *Hieroglyphica Sacra*, or Divine Emblems in Thirteen Figures with Explanations.

<margin>XXVI—XXXIV.</margin>
3. *Sixteen Conferences*, concerning the Modern Doctrine of Election or Predestination. Illustrated with Symbols. In 8 Vols. Wherein the subject is fundamentally resolved, according to the Central Philosophy of J. B. A.D. 1715?

<note>One chief importance of this Work consists in the comprehensive and clear elucidation of the Seven Properties of Nature, with its Two Co-eternal Principles, of black Darkness and lustrous Light, having the Fire, or Life of each opened in the midst, being the Eye of the Supernatural, omnipotent Abyssal Will. This is contained in the Third to Ninth Conferences.</note>

4. *Five Conferences*, concerning the Absolute Necessity of all the Holy Sufferings, and Death of Jesus Christ, upon the Cross. With a large Hieroglyphical Figure, representing the Process of Christ in the Redemption of Humanity. <note>One thick volume unfinished.</note> A.D. 1716?

5. *Microcosmos*, or Man, the living Image or Form of the Deity, as in Himself supernaturally, and as manifested by Nature, in its Three Principles. Considered in his Primeval State, his Fallen State, and his State of Regeneration and full Deification. <note>One thick volume.</note> Being an Explanation of Three Symbolic Folding Tables.

<note>This work was composed before all the other Treatises, but the author's enlarged knowledge in subsequent years led him to make considerable improvements in the explanation of the First Table, which were carried out in A.D. 1717.</note>

And thirdly, as After the Last Judgment Day. (In the German language.) In Four Conferences. Written to clear up a doubt regarding the last treatise. ### POSTSCRIPT—ON METHODIST EVANGELISM.

## **EDUCATION in the Science of Spiritual Nature, or Theosophy, and its Practical Elucidations, Ancient and Modern, of Natural and Divine Magic, etc., the Way to Perfect the Spirit of Methodism as an Evangelical Agency.**

[Being a quotation from the body of the work from which the preceding extracts are taken; and referring to the series of studies on pages xvii–xxiii above.]

> "The specific purposes of these selections of books will be found described next to each one. By properly reading and studying them in the order in which they are set forth, the candidate may have his mind thoroughly imbued with the perfect principles of evangelical sanctity—free from biased, abusive, sectarian dogmas and opinions. For he is recommended to overlook all purely Roman Catholic, and indeed Protestant, doctrinal peculiarities, crudities, and idiosyncrasies that he may encounter in his research, and simply extract from each work the pure Christian honey and edifying instruction contained within. We may remark that such a level of qualification is necessary, not only to do justice to the personal and other subjects of the memorial, but also regarding the world at large. This is because the work is intended to become a kind of standard textbook of divine science—both elementary and recondite—in all its solid theoretical and practical diversities for future ages, complete with rules and directions for its full attainment, all presented in the purest classic simplicity.
> "One very important result we may mention, expected from the proposed work if properly executed, will be the refinement and exaltation of the *spirit of Methodism*, which is undeniably the most advanced system of popular evangelism that this country, the American continent, and the world at large have ever witnessed. By this, however, we also mean the spirit of religious philanthropy that is now so universally active (having been instrumentally originated by it), as well as the religious principles more specifically designated by that name. This system of simple, practical Gospel doctrine, and of preaching and applying the same—being *blended*, so to speak, with the extensive and diverse learning and experiences of the *great masters of spiritual science from former ages*, of the ancient philosophical as well as Christian *mystic* schools, and further refined by the maturing light of *theosophy* and the revelations of modern *experimental transcendentalism* (including both *divine* and *natural magic*)—may no longer remain a mere elementary and dogmatic theology. Such a theology is suited only for the masses of our own country or heathen lands, who can receive and believe without rational proof, and who are mostly incapable of logical and metaphysical research—that is, of tracing all the outcomes of a conclusion back to its premises, or the perfect development of the premises into the conclusion, so as to know with certainty that the beginning and the end are one; and further, of discerning whether the offered and received doctrines of faith, in all their parts and complexities, are in harmony or identical with natural and infallible abstract truth. Instead, we say, it will be exalted into a **perfect philosophy, or complete logical science.** And this will prove and recommend itself by the highest demonstration—not only through rational explanation based on the ground of nature and a clear interpretation of the signatures and forms of its *scientific properties and qualities* in its plant life, but also by the display and evidence of a complete mastery over all the manifested powers of the dark principle. This mastery transmutes, by a touch (or by a mere act of the will upon a properly prepared subject), all their predominant evil qualities into nothing but a more sublime vitality. All these *divine magical powers* were continually referred to by our Lord as the natural prerogatives of his faithful, theosophic, and perfect disciples after the redemption and glorification of humanity; he confirmed them after his resurrection from the dead, as summarized at the close of St. Mark's Gospel. Then, we say, the Gospel may be rightly and fully preached, and no rational mind (whether from the East or the West), upon hearing it (*Romans 10:8–17*), shall be able to deny or resist believing it. Then, as we have observed, missionaries may go forth who are capable of meeting the honest objections and *just demands* of the most refined rationalist or stubborn skeptic by demonstrating (to his outward *senses* as well as to his understanding, soul, and spirit) the truths of the Christian faith and their identity with the universal voice of nature."—See BÖHME's *Mysterium Magnum*, especially Chapters xvi, lxvii, and xxx.

<summary>This postscript argues that integrating theosophy and ancient spiritual sciences into Methodism will transform it from a simple dogmatic theology into a "perfect philosophy" capable of convincing even the most skeptical rationalists. It suggests that this higher spiritual education will grant missionaries the "divine magical powers" promised by Christ, allowing them to demonstrate the truths of the Gospel through both reason and physical evidence.</summary>

### ADVERTISEMENT.

Recently Published, in royal 18mo, wide margins, 512 pages, (price 10s. 6d.),

**AN INTRODUCTION TO THEOSOPHY, OR THE SCIENCE OF THE** "mystery of
CHRIST," that is, of Deity, Nature, and Creature, (*Colossians 1:15–20.*) Embracing the Philosophy of all the Working Powers of Life, Magical and Spiritual. And forming a Practical Guide to the Sublimest Purity, Sanctity, and Evangelical Perfection. Also, to the Attainment of Divine Vision, and all holy Angelical Arts, Powers, and other Prerogatives of the Regeneration.—*Volume 1. Complete in itself.* London: John Kendrick, 27, Ludgate Street.

**DEDICATION.**—To the Students of the Universities, Colleges, and Schools of Christendom. To Professors of Metaphysical, Mechanical, and Natural Science in all its forms. To Men and Women of fundamentally Orthodox Faith. To Deists, Arians, Unitarians, Swedenborgians, Arminians, Swedenborgians <note>The original text repeats this name; it likely refers to various branches of the sect or is a printing error.</note>, and other Defective and Ungrounded Creeds, Rationalists and Skeptics of Every Kind. To Just-Minded and Enlightened Muslims, Jews, and Oriental Patriarch-Religionists. But especially, To the Gospel Minister and Missionary (whether to the Barbaric or the Intellectual Peoples)—This Introduction to Theosophy, or the Science of the Ground and Mystery of all Things, is most Humbly and Affectionately Dedicated.

---

Note.—A Copy of this Volume has been presented and forwarded to every Missionary of the Four great London Societies (the *Society for the Propagation of the Gospel, the Church Missionary Society, the Wesleyan Methodist Missionary Society, and the London Missionary Society*) laboring in India and Ceylon—as offering to them the clue to the true and only means of bringing the intellectual Hindu and Muslim nations (out of their own patriarchal or natural religious foundations) into the evangelical faith of Christianity. A Copy has also been presented to every major College, Roman Catholic and Protestant, throughout Great Britain and Ireland, as well as to upwards of Forty principal Colleges and Libraries of the United States. This is done with a view to direct the studies and researches of the present rising and future generations to the true philosophy of Nature and Christianity, as revealed in the writings of LAW, BÖHME, and FREHER, as well as to the perfect practice and attainment of spiritual Regeneration. And further, it serves as a guide to the only safe way by which enlightened Christian minds may approach the modern revived sciences of *Animal* or *Vital Magnetism* and Magic, with their wondrous *secrets* (arcana) henceforth to be revealed. When this philosophy shall be duly understood, then 'the end will come' of the Babel-like confusion of theological opinions, and 'there shall be one fold and one shepherd.' *John 10:16.*

---

In the Preface to this Volume, it is observed, alluding to the modern '*experimental transcendentalisms*' of *Animal Magnetism*, *Clairvoyance*, etc.: —"For the requirement for progress in supersensual science is thereby supplied, and the revelations of the magical or spiritual ground of nature by true divine media—'*children of the mystery*,' subjects of the *high regeneration*, and theosophic *magi*—may henceforth far surpass in sublimity of character and beneficial results to the world the discoveries of the laws, powers, and properties of material nature." In reference to this point also, the following further quotation is inserted here:

"Around the sixteenth volume of the Course (*'INTRODUCTION TO THEOSOPHY'*), FREHER'S *WRITINGS* might commence, which would probably occupy about twenty-six volumes. Next after these, some judicious treatises on *ANIMAL MAGNETISM* might be presented, setting forth in proper classification its various recorded and known phenomena, of both body and mind, and also in respect to the instinctive and inanimate creation. These would then indicate the ground and mystery of the same, with suggestions for further research and experiment, all according to the established principles, properties, and laws of nature, as described in the previously given theosophical treatises, and showing how this wonderful but as yet undeveloped—nay, unrecognized—discovery of these last ages (of *Animal* or *Vital Magnetism*) has always been the great *experimental requirement* of Theosophy, though alluded to and prophesied about by its grand masters in their *writings* as an event that should assuredly arrive and be continually expected. When, indeed, the *WRITINGS* of BÖHME—or rather the mysteries of Wisdom and Truth so wonderfully contained in them—should be made understandable to every rightly prepared subject and artist; indeed, when greater works or wonders of pure natural and evangelical truth than any he had recorded (not of *Swedenborgian*, *Cahagnetic*, *Davison*, and such similar mere *astral phantoms*) should be open to contemplation, at the will and direction of the controlling and rightly qualified magus. . . .

"The chief practical end, then, of these last proposed volumes in the Course would be the faithful explanation of the art by which humanity, in respect to its moral or divine nature, may be magically freed from its <term>saturnine constringency</term> <note>A Böhmean term referring to the restrictive, dark, or "cold" properties of unredeemed nature.</note>, pollution, and deadness (as implied in the mandatory requirements of our Lord's doctrine in order to realize his salvation), and then powerfully introduced into the birth, element, and qualities of the *spirit of love*, or its original and redeemed inward perfection. This, it is admitted, is the end of common Christianity, but the Church, as such, no longer possessing the power of the *keys* or high advancement in divine science and art, is no longer able to achieve this as contemplated in the Gospel. This implies that the true disciple or perfect believer in Christ shall be inwardly as his glorified head and Lord, and shall manifest that refined exaltation of nature by corresponding works, wisdom, and power.

"We might also refer to the glorious benefits of such a *divine art* in respect to Education, in opening and *strengthening the intellectual powers* (that is, by the infusion of wisdom and knowledge into the liberated intellect during the *magical sleep*, etc.), but we shall conclude these remarks with merely repeating that the object of these last volumes in the Course would be to apply to a proper Gospel purpose—in such a position and relation, and after a further adequate development of it—the glorious rediscovery, philosophy, and phenomena of *Animal or Mental Magnetism*, *Spiritism*, etc.; in other words, of the *NATURAL and DIVINE MAGIC*. (*Myster. Magn. 68:7.*)"

<summary>This page contains the bibliographic record and title description for Christopher Walton’s 1854 collection of materials intended for a biography of William Law, which also examines the work of Jacob Böhme and Dionysius Andreas Freher. It notes that the book was a limited private edition of 500 copies and contains handwritten insertions.</summary>
